clue.text: Very little deprecation Noah broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of the two words are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: Noah preaching gloom across the land barely registered with anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a quantity so tiny relative to the whole that it hardly counts, i.e. very little.

clue.text: Regrettably pursuing extremely nasty beasts

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the regrettable word comes after the other piece
extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters, of the word nasty

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning regrettably

explanation.surface: Some sorry pack of vicious animals chasing after something nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Nyalas are spiral-horned African antelopes, so they are an example of beasts.

clue.text: Zero charge for this sapling, reportedly? Over my dead body

indicators.note: reportedly says the words are to be heard rather than read as spelt

parts.note: a sapling is a new tree, which sounds like the first part of the answer
over my dead body is an emphatic refusal, i.e. no

explanation.surface: Someone vows to fight off anyone trying to charge nothing for a young tree.
explanation.definitionFit: This subatomic particle is electrically neutral, so it is the thing that carries zero charge.

clue.text: Female advisor's visit frequently unintroduced

indicators.note: unintroduced means without its opening, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: to haunt a place is to visit it frequently

explanation.surface: A woman's counsellor keeps dropping by without being announced.
explanation.walkthrough: An agony aunt is a newspaper columnist who answers readers' personal problems, hence a female advisor.
explanation.definitionFit: A relative of a parent's generation, and in the agony-column sense a woman who gives advice.

clue.text: Dark, violent criminal supporting chief of Klan, a high rank

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed underneath, so these pieces follow the first
chief of means the leading letter of the word Klan

parts.note: night is the dark part of the day
a hood is a hoodlum, a violent criminal

explanation.surface: A thug backing a Klan leader reaches a lofty position in its hierarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being made a knight is an honour conferring an elevated title and status, a high rank.

clue.text: Tank appearing in intermittently macabre film

indicators.note: appearing in says one piece sits inside the other
intermittently means taking every other letter of the word macabre

parts.note: a vat is a large tank for liquids

explanation.surface: An armoured vehicle turns up now and then in a gruesome movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tank' suggests the armoured vehicle, but here it is a storage vessel for liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Avatar is James Cameron's 2009 science-fiction blockbuster, an example of a film.

clue.text: Russian involved in dismissal by American firm

indicators.note: involved in says one piece is wrapped inside the other

parts.note: RO is the cricket abbreviation for run out, a way a batter is dismissed
Igor is a typical Russian man's name
US is short for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: A Russian is caught up in being sacked by a US company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a company noun beside American, but it is the adjective defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something strict, exacting and unyielding, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Entranced elite working to secure old understanding

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast inside, so one piece encloses the other
working means operating or in motion, so the letters are set moving into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A spellbound upper class labours to lock down some ancient pact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to secure' means the old letter is held inside the rearranged letters, not placed at an end.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1904 Anglo-French agreement was a friendly diplomatic pact, an understanding between nations.

clue.text: Cheap passage from Scots port in the midst of thunderous wind

indicators.note: in says the port sits inside the two middle letters
the midst of means the central letters of the ten-letter word thunderous

parts.note: Ayr is a port on the west coast of Scotland
to wind is to turn, as a road winds

explanation.surface: Sailing from a Scottish harbour into a howling gale.
explanation.walkthrough: Thunderous has ten letters, so its midst is a pair of letters rather than one.
explanation.definitionFit: A British rail ticket for going and coming back within one day at a reduced fare, so a cheap passage.

clue.text: Slang is viewed, partly upon reflection, as an insult

indicators.note: upon reflection says the hidden letters are read backwards
partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Street slang, when you think it over, comes across as offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upon reflection' turns the run found across the three words back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-fingered gesture with the palm inward is a rude British insult.

clue.text: Bird in wet-look having agreed to go out

indicators.note: to go marks the agreed letters leaving, and out says what remains is rearranged

parts.note: OK means agreed

explanation.surface: A bird in a glossy wet-look style that everyone agreed on is heading out.
explanation.walkthrough: WETLOOK loses OK, and the remaining WETLO is shuffled to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A young owl is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Risky middle course one is taught, reportedly, during negotiation

definitions.meaning: a precarious path between two extremes, a balancing act

definitions.text: one is taught, reportedly, during negotiation
definitions.meaning: a funambulist's cable is taut, which sounds like taught, while it is being negotiated or crossed

explanation.surface: A dangerous compromise someone learns during bargaining talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negotiation' suggests bargaining, but here it means crossing an obstacle; taught is said like taut.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively a delicate balancing path between extremes; literally a stretched cable a performer walks along.

clue.text: One ship crew turned out drunk in eastern port

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and disordered, so the letters are jumbled
turned out means emptied, as of a drawer, so only the outer letters of crew remain

explanation.surface: A sailor arrives tipsy in an East Coast harbour after the crew is thrown off.
explanation.walkthrough: CREW emptied leaves CW; I, SHIP and CW are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipswich, the county town of Suffolk, is a port on the Orwell estuary in eastern England.

clue.text: Elbow maybe half-trashing narcotic dive

indicators.note: half here takes the second half of the eight-letter word trashing

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a dive is a seedy bar or club, also called a joint

explanation.surface: Someone half wrecks a druggy drinking den.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half of trashing is HING.
explanation.definitionFit: The elbow bends one way like a door on its hinges, so it is an example of this kind of articulation.

clue.text: Remove tutu for altering

indicators.note: altering means changing, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Take out a ballet skirt to have it adjusted.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw someone out unceremoniously is to eject or remove them.

clue.text: Film consisted of ghoul regularly worried about foreign character

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters go round the other piece
worried means agitated, so the letters are churned into a new order
regularly takes every other letter of the word ghoul, here the second and fourth

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A movie made up of a fretful monster circling an alien figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consisted of' looks like a link phrase but is the bulk of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1965 Rodgers and Hammerstein musical starring Julie Andrews is a famous film.

clue.text: Thorny religious image of community swinging both ways with maiden in short bonnet

parts.note: EC is the European Community

indicators.note: swinging both ways says the piece is given forwards and then backwards

parts.note: the same EC for European Community, used a second time

indicators.note: in says the maiden goes inside the shortened headgear
short means cut off at the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a hood is a soft bonnet-like head covering
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A spiky devotional picture of a bisexual group with a girl in a cut-down hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims HOOD to HOO and M goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'behold the man', it is a painting of Christ crowned with thorns, a religious image.

clue.text: Trifles — best to come up in a little while

indicators.note: in says the reversed piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a minute is a little while

indicators.note: in a down clue, to come up means read upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: A1 means first-class or best, with the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Small things: the top choice will surface shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean small, trivial details or matters of little importance.

clue.text: Subject, shunning society, getting caught in isolated group

indicators.note: in says the caught letter goes inside what remains
shunning means avoiding, so the society letter is dropped

parts.note: to subject a people is to enslave them
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A subject avoiding social life gets trapped in a cut-off clique.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinct community or territory surrounded by a different one is an isolated group or area.

clue.text: After a birthday, initially forwarded present? No

indicators.note: after says the forwarded piece comes behind the others
initially means the opening letter of the word birthday

parts.note: sent means forwarded, as of mail

explanation.surface: A birthday gift that was posted on but never arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present? No' is the opposite of present, so it defines the answer as not here.
explanation.definitionFit: Not present means away or missing, the antonym of being in attendance.

clue.text: French ways rejected by mostly cold and slimy performer

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: dank means unpleasantly cold and damp

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: rues are French streets

explanation.surface: French streets rejected by some clammy, chilly entertainer.
explanation.definitionFit: A male ballet dancer, so a kind of performer.

clue.text: Prettiest heroine, some might have it?

definitions.text: Prettiest heroine, some might have it?

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some would say the loveliest heroine of all is this one.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'might have it' is no definition; the whole clue is the definition: some might name the Bible's beautiful queen as the prettiest heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical queen, chosen by the Persian king for her beauty, is a heroine whom some would call the prettiest.

clue.text: Connections in company headquarters cleared over withdrawn report

indicators.note: over says the emptied word stretches over the other piece
cleared means emptied, so only the outer letters of headquarters remain
withdrawn means pulled back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a report is a loud noise, like a gunshot

explanation.surface: Links at a firm's head office are severed after a leaked report is withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' suggests a document, but here it is the bang of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Cohesions are bonds that hold things together, i.e. links or connections.

clue.text: Six into nine hundred — initially use a calculator for it?

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: Dividing six into nine hundred: better reach for a calculator.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyperbolic sine is a mathematical function usually worked out with a scientific calculator key.

clue.text: Exclamation of rebuke one laid on South African

parts.note: tut is a sound of disapproval
one is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A tut-tut with a scolding directed at someone from South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tutsi are a people of Rwanda and Burundi, so one is an African.

clue.text: Government taking months to stop a boom?

indicators.note: to stop means to plug, so the months letter goes inside the noise

parts.note: a boom is a loud din

explanation.surface: The authorities take months to halt an economic upswing.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for administration, the governing body or management, hence government.

clue.text: Forward has to shave — nothing about missing a match

indicators.note: about says the nothing word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: nil means nothing
on means forward, as in moving on
to pare is to shave or trim

explanation.surface: A footballer must trim his beard before a nil-nil game without a rival.
explanation.definitionFit: Something peerless has no equal, so it lacks any rival or match.
